title: Beyond Calabrese-Cardy Scaling: Exceptional-Point Sensitivity from the de Sitter RT Surface
abstract: In non-Hermitian critical chains near exceptional points, the biorthogonal entanglement entropy of a finite system retains sensitivity to a small energy gap Delta even when Delta < 1/L. On top of the usual Calabrese-Cardy term there is an interval-independent contribution S_res = log(Delta*L), visible as a vertical offset and detectable even for a one-site subsystem. This has no Hermitian analogue: a sub-finite-size gap is effectively invisible to entanglement in unitary critical chains. The result is interpreted within the de Sitter geometry generated by non-unitary continuous MERA: because the dS extremal surface reaches the IR endpoint, entanglement necessarily retains the endpoint contribution. On a finite ring a regular circuit cannot terminate at a one-site product state and instead leaves an entangled two-site IR state; computing the entanglement of that IR state recovers the same log(Delta*L) term, identifying the extra long-range entanglement as residual entropy left after finite-depth disentangling.
key_claims: Biorthogonal entanglement entropy near an exceptional point carries an interval-independent residual term S_res = log(Delta*L) beyond Calabrese-Cardy scaling.
The effect has no Hermitian analogue: in unitary critical chains a sub-finite-size gap (Delta < 1/L) is invisible to entanglement.
The term is explained geometrically by the non-unitary cMERA de Sitter bulk, whose extremal (RT) surface reaches the IR endpoint rather than terminating in the interior.
On a finite ring a regular MERA-like circuit cannot disentangle to a one-site product state; the residual entangled two-site IR state reproduces the same log(Delta*L) contribution.
relevance_note: Direct follow-up by the same author (Chou) to arXiv:2606.17983 (Chou-Chang), which is PAPER-2026-119 and the SEED for HYP-2026-028. It advances exactly the route our own HYP-028 result notes designated as the way forward after the exact-diagonalization route was closed by SIM-053/055: a non-Hermitian tensor-network (cMERA) construction rather than bigger ED. Two concrete uses. (1) DIAGNOSTIC: S_res = log(Delta*L) is a cheap, interval-independent, single-site-detectable observable that could serve as a regime/criticality indicator in the non-Hermitian setting, complementing (not replacing) the mandatory G4 gate (c_eff = 2/5, Delta_phi = -1/5). (2) STRUCTURAL WARNING for our own circuits: the claim that a regular circuit on a finite ring cannot terminate in a one-site product state and leaves an entangled two-site IR state is a statement about finite-depth MERA IR termination in general, i.e. about the top of the causal cone our force and OPE pipelines contract through. HONEST LIMIT: this paper does NOT supply a non-unitary fixed point with documented CFT data sitting at finite distance inside the PT-unbroken window, so it does NOT by itself unblock HYP-028's G4 criticality gate -- it works near exceptional points, which is the same PT-edge neighborhood that obstructed SIM-053/055. It is a route strengthener and a diagnostic source, not a solution to the reachability obstruction.
anchor_contradiction: None. The claimed effect is explicitly stated to have NO Hermitian analogue, so it does not bear on our unitary-chain anchors (alpha = 2*Delta_T = 4 across Ising c=1/2, tricritical Ising c=7/10, Potts c=4/5; transport residual -1.2% at N=16; C_sigma-sigma-epsilon = 0.50 +/- 0.03; C_TTT = 3.9936 Ising). The IR-termination remark concerns finite-depth circuits generally but predicts no correction to Hermitian MERA observables.
